newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - April 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - April 8.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
Indian Express
BHARATIYA JANATA PARTY LEADERS DIFFER OVER STAKING CLAIM

The senior leadership of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) was divided on the question of government formation. While party chief L.K. Advani favoured the party to opt out of the race for office and press for polls, senior leader and former prime minister A.B. Vajpayee was keen on putting together a BJP-led coalition before plunging into a mid-term election. Party sources said despite Advani's strong opposition to making a second bid at government formation, Vajpayee felt the BJP had a chance, given the fear of elections among the constituents of the ruling coalition.
The Hindustan Times
UN MUST REFLECT THIRD WORLD'S CONCERNS

Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda called upon non-aligned countries to send out a message of collective resolve to support harmony and understanding, and denounce all forces of extremism, ethnic discord, separatism and terrorism. Inaugurating the 12th Non-Aligned Movement Ministerial Conference in New Delhi, Gowda said while globalisation was generally accepted as the direction of the future, it could not be equated with the interests of only the powerful economies and corporations. Globalisation, to be meaningful, must be accompanied by the empowerment of all economies, he said.
The Times Of India
TRUCKERS' STRIKE PUTS INDUSTRY, TRADE IN PERIL

Industrial production was slowly coming to a halt with the transporter's indefinite strike choking off goods movement to and from factories throughout the country for the seventh day. Negotiations resumed between senior Finance Ministry officials and truck operators' representatives in the presence of some members of the parliamentary standing committee on finance. INDIAN AIRLINES FLOATS GLOBAL TENDER FOR AIRCRAFT SALE

As part of its fleet renewal programme, Indian Airlines (IA) floated a global tender for the sale of three Airbus A-300 aircraft in its fold. This marked the first step by IA for the sale of its planes. Last month, it floated a global tender to buy five Airbus aircraft on dry lease. Both the tenders would close in May. The three aircraft up for sale are above 20 years in age and could not be operated in India under the Directorate General of Civil Aviation guidelines.
INDUSTRIAL GROWTH FALLS TO 8.3 PCT

A sharp slump in the growth rate of manufacturing sector coupled with a negative growth in mining during December pushed down overall industrial growth to 8.3 percent during the first three quarters of 1996/97 (April-March) as against 11.4 percent in the same period of 1995/96. As per the estimates of the Index of Industrial Production, industrial growth during December came down to 4.1 percent from 10.6 percent last year.
Business Standard
RAILWAYS HIKE FREIGHT RATES FOR ESSENTIAL ITEMS

Railway freight rates went up by 12 percent for essential commodities from April 1, 1997, despite assurance in the railway budget speech that essential commodities were exempted from the increase in freight rates. This hike was applicable to essential commodities like grains and pulses, oils, salt, onions, potato, sugar, vanaspati, jaggery and fodder. The freight hike would result in a corresponding increase in the prices of all essential commodities. Though the railway budget had not been passed by parliament, the authorities had started charging the revised freight rates from April 1.
WORLD BANK ADVICE TO DEVALUE RUPEE REJECTED

The World Bank's bid to influence India's farm policy suffered a setback, with the agriculture minister refusing to entertain its suggestions to devalue the rupee, lower import duty on edible oils and reduce farm subsidies. The suggestions were made by a World Bank policy mission during its meeting with the minister. The minister, however, agreed to consider suggestions to start projects assisted by the Bank for streamlining agricultural credit and improving productivity of small and marginal farms.
MOVE TO ALLOW FOREIGN INVESTOR CLIENT FUNDS INTO DEBT MARKET

The bourse regulator (SEBI) sought the Finance Ministry's assent to allow foreign institutional investors (FIIs) to take the proprietary funds route for investing client funds in the debt market. So far, FIIs were allowed to invest self-owned funds in the debt market. If cleared, this would allow individual foreign investors, not registered with SEBI as FIIs, into the debt market.
ANDHRA FIRST STATE TO GET DIRECT WORLD BANK LOAN

Andhra Pradesh was set to become the first state in the country to receive a structural adjustment loan directly from the World Bank. A loan of about 50 billion rupees had been arranged from the bank, the state chief minister said. This arrangement marked a significant departure from the existing procedure, which stipulated that all such loans should be routed through the Union government.
